title: Routes, Cloud NAT and Private Google Access

videos.script: Every packet that leaves a machine is matched against the network's routes. {{routes}} The most specific destination wins. Only between routes for the same range does priority count. {{specific}} One route is special: zero dot zero, to the default internet gateway. It is the way out of the network. {{default}} Delete it, and nothing leaves. Not to the internet, and not to Google's own APIs either, unless a route for their range stays. {{noway}} A machine with no external address can still reach out, through Cloud NAT. It can start connections. It can never accept them. {{nat}} There is no NAT machine to run. It is a setting on a Cloud Router, in one region, and its biggest cost is the data it processes. {{cost}} And Private Google Access is one line on a subnet. It lets those same machines reach Google's APIs, and nothing else. {{pga}} It opens no firewall, and it grants no permission. That is still IAM's job. {{end}}
